meanings: what is meant by the expression ...

components.note: 斤 (axe) — cutting tools, as in 新 new and 斩 chop. 所 once echoed the sound of chopping; "place" and "that which" are later borrowed uses.
讠 (speech) — 讠 is the simplified 言, as in 说, 话; 谓 is to call or say, as in 所谓.
胃 (wèi) — same sound — 谓 is wèi; 胃 also sounds out 渭 wèi.

example.hanzi: 这就是所谓的双赢局面。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiù shì suǒwèi de shuāngyíng júmiàn.
example.english: This is what's called a win-win situation.
example.fact: 所谓 can be entirely neutral, simply glossing a term before defining it ("所谓A,就是B" — "what is meant by A is B") — but placed directly before a noun in casual speech, it often tips into a skeptical or dismissive "so-called," the same slide English "so-called" makes from neutral definition to implied doubt.

examples.hanzi: 所谓朋友,就是在你难过时陪着你的人。
examples.pinyin: Suǒwèi péngyou, jiù shì zài nǐ nánguò shí péi zhe nǐ de rén.
examples.english: What we call a friend is someone who stays with you when you're sad.

examples.hanzi: 他所谓的好办法其实一点儿也不好。
examples.pinyin: Tā suǒwèi de hǎo bànfǎ qíshí yìdiǎnr yě bù hǎo.
examples.english: His so-called good idea is actually not good at all.

meanings: measure word for bolts of cloth

components.note: 匸 (a hiding box, open at the side) — the frame around 儿. Rare radical, not meaningful on its own.
儿 (legs) — the legs below. Memory aid: 匹 counts horses (一匹马) — think of a horse's legs under a covering, or a bolt of cloth rolled up.

example.pinyin: Cǎodì shang yǒu sān pǐ mǎ.
example.english: There are three horses on the grass.
example.fact: 匹 is the measure word for horses and bolts of cloth: 一匹马, 一匹布. It also means to match: 匹配 (to pair up) and 匹敌 (to be a match for). 单枪匹马 describes someone going it alone.

examples.hanzi: 他骑着一匹白马。
examples.pinyin: Tā qízhe yì pǐ báimǎ.
examples.english: He is riding a white horse.

examples.hanzi: 这两个人的水平很匹配。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng gè rén de shuǐpíng hěn pǐpèi.
examples.english: These two people are well matched in level.

components.note: 角 (horn, corner) — a picture of an animal horn. Read jiǎo for horn, corner and angle; jué for a role, as in 角色.

example.pinyin: Niú yǒu liǎng zhī jiǎo.
example.english: A cow has two horns.
example.fact: 角 is jiǎo for horn, corner and angle: 三角形 (triangle), 墙角 (corner). It is jué in 角色 (role) and 主角 (lead). In money, 一角 is a tenth of a yuan, spoken as 毛.

examples.hanzi: 我走到了街角，等你。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zǒu dào le jiējiǎo, děng nǐ.
examples.english: I walked to the corner of the street and waited for you.

examples.hanzi: 这个三角形的角是直角。
examples.pinyin: Zhège sānjiǎoxíng de jiǎo shì zhíjiǎo.
examples.english: The angle of this triangle is a right angle.

components.note: 廴 (long stride) — a rare radical of walking and extending, also in 延 yán and 廷 tíng; 建 means to set up or put up; the sound clue 聿 is only loose.
立 (stand) — a person standing on the ground line. As a radical it appears in 站 stand, 位 seat, 竟; also in 建立 establish.

example.hanzi: 两国正式建立了外交关系。
example.pinyin: Liǎng guó zhèngshì jiànlì le wàijiāo guānxi.
example.english: The two countries formally established diplomatic relations.
example.fact: 建立 pairs a construction verb, 建 ("to build," as in 建筑), with 立 ("to stand up, to erect") to mean "to build and stand up" something abstract — relationships, systems, organizations — treating an institution as if it were a physical structure being erected.

examples.hanzi: 我们要和邻居建立良好的关系。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào hé línjū jiànlì liánghǎo de guānxi.
examples.english: We should build good relationships with our neighbors.

examples.hanzi: 这家公司是在二十年前建立的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī shì zài èrshí nián qián jiànlì de.
examples.english: This company was founded twenty years ago.

components.note: 卩 (kneeling person) — a hand 爪 pressing on a person 卩: to stamp or press a mark, hence seal and print.

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhè zhāng zhǐ yìn chūlai.
example.english: Please print this sheet out.
example.fact: 印 means to press a mark: 印章 (seal, chop), 印象 (impression), 印刷 (printing). The same shape names a seal of authority, which is why 盖印 (to stamp) makes a document official. In computing 打印 means to print.

examples.hanzi: 请在这里盖一个印章。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài zhèlǐ gài yí gè yìnzhāng.
examples.english: Please stamp a seal here.

examples.hanzi: 他在纸上印了很多图案。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài zhǐ shang yìn le hěn duō tú'àn.
examples.english: He printed many patterns on the paper.

components.note: 無 (traditional) — began as a person dancing with ornaments (same root as 舞). 'None' is a borrowed sense; 无 is an old variant of 無 and the shape does not explain it.
斤 (axe) — cutting tools, as in 新 new and 斩 chop. 所 once echoed the sound of chopping; "place" and "that which" are later borrowed uses.
讠 (speech) — 讠 is the simplified 言, as in 说, 话; 谓 is to call or say, as in 所谓.
胃 (wèi) — same sound — 谓 is wèi; 胃 also sounds out 渭 wèi.

example.hanzi: 你想去哪儿都无所谓,我都可以。
example.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng qù nǎr dōu wú suǒwèi, wǒ dōu kěyǐ.
example.english: It doesn't matter to me where you want to go — I'm fine with anything.
example.fact: 无所谓 is literally 无 ("without") plus 所谓 (rank 1193 in this batch, "what is meant/called") — "there's nothing that could even be called [a problem]," a compositional path from "there's nothing to call it" to today's casual "whatever, I don't care."

examples.hanzi: 吃什么都无所谓,我不挑食。
examples.pinyin: Chī shénme dōu wúsuǒwèi, wǒ bù tiāoshí.
examples.english: I don't care what we eat, I'm not picky.

examples.hanzi: 他假装无所谓,其实心里很在意。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiǎzhuāng wúsuǒwèi, qíshí xīnlǐ hěn zàiyì.
examples.english: He pretends not to care, but he actually cares a lot.

components.note: 又 (hand) — the bottom, standing in for the 攴 (tap) of traditional 變. 亦 on top replaces the tangled-thread part and has no meaning link.
變 (traditional) — tangled threads and a tapping hand 攴: sorting out a mess, so 'change'. Read as 'usually explained'.
化 (change) — one person 亻 beside an upside-down person 匕 — a change of state; 化 is to change, as in 文化 and 变化.

example.hanzi: 这个城市这几年变化很大。
example.pinyin: Zhège chéngshì zhè jǐ nián biànhuà hěn dà.
example.english: This city has changed a lot in the past few years.
example.fact: 变化 combines two overlapping "change" characters — 变 ("to change, to transform," also seen in 变态, rank 1190 of this batch) and 化 ("to transform, to turn into," as in 文化 "culture") — another instance of Mandarin's common two-near-synonym compounding pattern.

examples.hanzi: 天气变化太快,小心感冒。
examples.pinyin: Tiānqì biànhuà tài kuài, xiǎoxīn gǎnmào.
examples.english: The weather changes quickly, so be careful not to catch a cold.

examples.hanzi: 他的心情随着天气的变化而变化。
examples.pinyin: Tā de xīnqíng suí zhe tiānqì de biànhuà ér biànhuà.
examples.english: His mood changes along with the weather.

components.note: 衣 (clothes; 衤 on the left) — the outer garment.
毛 (fur) — a fur coat worn outside: the outside, the surface, then to show.
辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 达 is to get through to, to reach.
大 (dà) is only a loose stand-in for the old sound part, so treat it as a rough clue for dá.

example.hanzi: 她不太会用语言表达自己的感情。
example.pinyin: Tā bú tài huì yòng yǔyán biǎodá zìjǐ de gǎnqíng.
example.english: She isn't very good at expressing her feelings in words.
example.fact: 表 ("outer surface," from a fur garment traditionally worn on the outside) plus 达 ("to reach, to arrive at") combine into "to bring something inner out to the surface and have it arrive [at another person]" — a vivid two-step image of communication as surfacing and delivering an inner feeling.

examples.hanzi: 请用简单的话表达你的想法。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng yòng jiǎndān de huà biǎodá nǐ de xiǎngfǎ.
examples.english: Please express your thoughts in simple words.

examples.hanzi: 他向她表达了感谢。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiàng tā biǎodá le gǎnxiè.
examples.english: He expressed his thanks to her.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and binding, as in 红, 给, 经: an agreement binds like a cord.
勺 (sháo) is a loose sound clue for yuē; 勺 also in 药 yào and 钓 diào.

example.hanzi: 从这里到机场大约要一个小时。
example.pinyin: Cóng zhèlǐ dào jīchǎng dàyuē yào yí gè xiǎoshí.
example.english: It takes about an hour to get from here to the airport.
example.fact: 约 alone already carries the sense of "approximately, to arrange an appointment" (as in 约会, "a date") — pairing it with 大 ("roughly, broadly") in 大约 reinforces the vagueness, making it Mandarin's default hedge word before a number, much like English "about" or "roughly."

examples.hanzi: 这家店大约晚上九点关门。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn dàyuē wǎnshang jiǔ diǎn guānmén.
examples.english: This shop closes at about nine in the evening.

examples.hanzi: 我大约三年前来过这里。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ dàyuē sān nián qián lái guo zhèlǐ.
examples.english: I came here about three years ago.

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
车 (cart) — 车 is a cart; 辈 first meant rows of war carts, hence ranks and generations.
非 (fēi) — near sound — 辈 is bèi; 非 also sounds out 悲 bēi and 排 pái.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 他一辈子都住在这个小镇上。
example.pinyin: Tā yí bèizi dōu zhù zài zhège xiǎozhèn shàng.
example.english: He has lived in this small town his whole life.
example.fact: 辈子 literally means "a generation" (辈 originally described a row of chariots traveling together, later extended to "a generation of people") — 一辈子, "one generation['s worth of time]," became the standard way to say "a whole lifetime," distinct from the near-synonym 一生, which is built instead from 生 ("to be born, life").

examples.hanzi: 她一辈子都没出过远门。
examples.pinyin: Tā yí bèizi dōu méi chū guo yuǎnmén.
examples.english: She never traveled far in her whole life.

examples.hanzi: 这是我一辈子最难忘的一天。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ yí bèizi zuì nánwàng de yì tiān.
examples.english: This is the most unforgettable day of my life.

components.note: 东 (east) — simplified from 東; a common memory aid is the sun 日 caught in a tree 木 at sunrise.

example.pinyin: Tàiyáng cóng dōngbian shēngqǐ.
example.english: The sun rises in the east.
example.fact: 东西 is dōngxī for "east and west" but dōngxi (neutral tone) for "thing", a famous pair. 房东 (landlord) and 东道主 (host) come from the idea of the host sitting on the east side.

examples.hanzi: 我家在学校的东边。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā zài xuéxiào de dōngbian.
examples.english: My home is east of the school.

examples.hanzi: 他去过东京三次。
examples.pinyin: Tā qù guo Dōngjīng sān cì.
examples.english: He has been to Tokyo three times.

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical; 仅 is the simplified form of 僅.
又 (yòu) — in the old form 僅 the sound came from 堇 (jǐn); 仅 and 谨 jǐn sound the same.
亻 (person) — person radical; 仅 is the simplified form of 僅.
又 (yòu) — in the old form 僅 the sound came from 堇 (jǐn); 仅 and 谨 jǐn sound the same.

example.hanzi: 他仅仅用了三天就完成了这个项目。
example.pinyin: Tā jǐnjǐn yòng le sān tiān jiù wánchéng le zhège xiàngmù.
example.english: He completed this project in just three days.
example.fact: 仅仅 is just 仅 ("only, merely") reduplicated for emphasis, tightening the scope of "only" even further than 仅 alone — the same intensifying-through-reduplication strategy seen in 谢谢, which likewise doubles a single syllable.

examples.hanzi: 我仅仅是想问你一个问题。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jǐnjǐn shì xiǎng wèn nǐ yí ge wèntí.
examples.english: I just wanted to ask you one question.

examples.hanzi: 这仅仅是个开始,后面还有更多。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jǐnjǐn shì ge kāishǐ, hòumiàn hái yǒu gèng duō.
examples.english: This is only the beginning, there's more to come.

components.note: 化 (huà) — near sound — 华 is huá; 化 also changes tone to sound out 华.
十 (ten) — the bottom 十 is a simplified remnant; 华 is flowery and splendid, as in 中华.
皿 (dish) — 皿 is a dish, as in 盘, 盖, 盒; 盛 is to fill a dish, then abundant.
成 (chéng) — near sound — 盛 is shèng; 成 also sounds out 城 chéng and 诚 chéng.
页 (head) — 页 is the head, as in 题, 顶, 领; 顿 is to bow the head and then pause.
屯 (tún) — near sound — 顿 is dùn; 屯 also sounds out 钝 dùn and 炖 dùn.

example.hanzi: 乔治·华盛顿是美国的第一位总统。
example.pinyin: Qiáozhì Huáshèngdùn shì Měiguó de dìyī wèi zǒngtǒng.
example.english: George Washington was the first president of the United States.
example.fact: 华盛顿 is the standard Mandarin transliteration for the name/place "Washington" — built by choosing characters purely for their sound (华 huá, 盛 shèng, 顿 dùn) rather than their literal meaning ("splendid", "abundant", "pause"), the same phonetic-borrowing strategy behind 乔治 ("George", also in this batch, rank 1221).

examples.hanzi: 我下个月要去华盛顿出差。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xià ge yuè yào qù Huáshèngdùn chūchāi.
examples.english: I'm going to Washington on a business trip next month.

examples.hanzi: 华盛顿的春天有很多樱花。
examples.pinyin: Huáshèngdùn de chūntiān yǒu hěn duō yīnghuā.
examples.english: There are many cherry blossoms in Washington in spring.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 造 is to go and make something.
告 (gào) is a loose sound clue (-ao); also in 浩 hào, 靠 kào.

example.pinyin: Zhè liàng chē shì zài Zhōngguó zào de.
example.english: This car was made in China.
example.fact: 造 is to make something, including abstractions: 造句 (to make a sentence), 造成 (to cause, used for bad results). It also forms 制造 (to manufacture), 创造 (to create) and 造型 (modelling, styling).

examples.hanzi: 他们在城东造了一座新桥。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zài chéng dōng zào le yí zuò xīn qiáo.
examples.english: They built a new bridge in the east of the city.

examples.hanzi: 这个杯子是手工制造的。
examples.pinyin: Zhège bēizi shì shǒugōng zhìzào de.
examples.english: This cup was made by hand.

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 好.
且 (qiě) is a loose sound clue for jiě; 且 also sounds out 祖 zǔ, 租 zū and 助 zhù.
女 (woman) — female relatives: 妈, 姐, 姑; 妹 is a younger sister.
未 (wèi) is close to mèi; also in 味 wèi.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen shì hǎo jiěmèi.
example.english: We are close sisters.
example.fact: 姐妹 strings together "older sister" (姐) and "younger sister" (妹) into one word covering "sisters" as a group, regardless of birth order — the same additive strategy behind 兄弟 ("brothers", elder brother + younger brother), since Chinese kinship terms build outward from specific relative ages rather than one generic "sibling" word.

examples.hanzi: 她们是亲姐妹,长得很像。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen shì qīn jiěmèi, zhǎng de hěn xiàng.
examples.english: They are real sisters and look alike.

examples.hanzi: 我有两个姐妹,一个在北京,一个在上海。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒu liǎng ge jiěmèi, yí ge zài Běijīng, yí ge zài Shànghǎi.
examples.english: I have two sisters, one in Beijing and one in Shanghai.

components.note: 礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — gods, rites and blessings: 礼 ritual, 福 fortune, 祝 wish; here 神 god or spirit.
申 (shēn) gives the sound (shén, tone differs); also in 伸 shēn stretch and 绅 shēn.
必 (bì) is a close sound clue for mì; 必 also gives 密 mì and 蜜 mì.

example.pinyin: Zhège dǎoyǔ fēicháng shénmì.
example.english: This island is very mysterious.
example.fact: 神 ("god, spirit") combines with 秘 ("secret") to give 神秘 an almost otherworldly sense of hidden secrecy; 秘 itself, per its own semantic component 禾 ("grain"), is traditionally linked to grain once kept out of sight, before the character's meaning narrowed to just "secret."

examples.hanzi: 她身上有一种神秘的气质。
examples.pinyin: Tā shēn shang yǒu yì zhǒng shénmì de qìzhì.
examples.english: She has a mysterious air about her.

examples.hanzi: 他的过去一直是个神秘的故事。
examples.pinyin: Tā de guòqù yìzhí shì ge shénmì de gùshi.
examples.english: His past has always been a mystery.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室: a house stocked with goods, so solid and real.
王 (jade) — on the left, 王 is the jade radical, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 理 reason; jade is bright and shows itself.
见 (jiàn, see) is a close sound clue (xiàn) and also fits the meaning: appear so it can be seen.

example.hanzi: 他终于把自己的梦想实现了。
example.pinyin: Tā zhōngyú bǎ zìjǐ de mèngxiǎng shíxiàn le.
example.english: He finally made his own dream a reality.
example.fact: 现 (built from 见 "to see" catching sight of a valuable 王/玉 "jade") contributes a sense of "to appear, to manifest" — 实现 pairs "to make real" with "to manifest," capturing the idea of turning something abstract, like a plan or a dream, into a visible reality.

examples.hanzi: 只要努力,你一定能实现目标。
examples.pinyin: Zhǐyào nǔlì, nǐ yídìng néng shíxiàn mùbiāo.
examples.english: As long as you work hard, you can definitely achieve your goal.

examples.hanzi: 这个想法很好,但很难实现。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiǎngfǎ hěn hǎo, dàn hěn nán shíxiàn.
examples.english: This idea is good, but hard to realize.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — cloth family: 布, 带, 帽. Memory aid: a market stall with a cloth banner 巾 under a roof 亠, i.e. a 市 market.
柿 (shì, persimmon) — contains 市 as a sound part, same sound shì.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen qù chāoshì mǎi cài.
example.english: We are going to the supermarket to buy groceries.
example.fact: 市 is a city and a market: 超市, 市场, 市民 (citizens). It also names the traditional "market" units, as in 市斤 (500 g), which is still used for shopping in China.

examples.hanzi: 这个城市有很多大市场。
examples.pinyin: Zhège chéngshì yǒu hěn duō dà shìchǎng.
examples.english: This city has many large markets.

examples.hanzi: 市里的公园很干净。
examples.pinyin: Shì lǐ de gōngyuán hěn gānjìng.
examples.english: The parks in the city are very clean.

components.note: 目 (eye) — 目 marks the eye and looking, as in 看, 眼, 睛; 瞧 is to look.
焦 (jiāo) — near sound — 瞧 is qiáo; 焦 also sounds out 憔 qiáo.
目 (eye) — 目 marks the eye and looking, as in 看, 眼, 睛; 瞧 is to look.
焦 (jiāo) — near sound — 瞧 is qiáo; 焦 also sounds out 憔 qiáo.

example.pinyin: Nǐ lái qiáoqiao zhège dōngxi.
example.english: Come take a look at this thing.
example.fact: 瞧瞧 doubles the verb 瞧 ("to look") the same way 谢谢 doubles 谢 ("to thank") — reduplicating a one-syllable action verb like this makes it sound light and casual, "just a quick look," with the second syllable typically toneless in speech.

examples.hanzi: 你瞧瞧,这个孩子又长高了。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ qiáoqiao, zhège háizi yòu zhǎng gāo le.
examples.english: Look at that, this child has grown taller again.

examples.hanzi: 让我瞧瞧你的新手机。
examples.pinyin: Ràng wǒ qiáoqiao nǐ de xīn shǒujī.
examples.english: Let me take a look at your new phone.

components.note: 攵 (tap, hand with stick) — acts that direct others: 教 teach, 放 release, 改 change, 收 collect; 政 is governing.
正 (zhèng) is the same sound; fits the sense too — government puts things right.
氵 (water radical, 三点水) — liquids and flow: 河, 汤, 酒; 治 first meant controlling water, then governing and curing.
台 (tái) is only a loose sound hint; the same part is in 始 shǐ and 胎 tāi.

example.pinyin: Tā duì zhèngzhì hěn gǎn xìngqù.
example.english: He is very interested in politics.
example.fact: 政 (attaching 攵, "a hand with a rod," to 正, "correct, upright") pictures enforcing correct order by force — governing — while 治 (water 氵 plus a platform 台) originally meant directing a river's flow; 政治 fuses "governing people" with "managing, controlling" into the modern word for "politics."

examples.hanzi: 他从小就不关心政治。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù bù guānxīn zhèngzhì.
examples.english: He has never cared about politics since he was little.

examples.hanzi: 这位政治家每天都很忙。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi zhèngzhìjiā měi tiān dōu hěn máng.
examples.english: This politician is busy every day.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, from 糸) — marks thread and ties, as in 线, 红, 约; 维 is a rope that holds things together.
隹 (zhuī, short-tailed bird) is only a loose sound clue for wéi, as in 推 tuī and 谁 shéi.

example.pinyin: Jǐngchá fùzé wéichí zhìxù.
example.english: The police are responsible for keeping order.
example.fact: 维 began as a rope that holds things together, and it gives 维持 (to maintain), 维护 (to safeguard), 维修 (to repair) and 维生素 (vitamin). 三维 means three-dimensional and 思维 means thinking.

examples.hanzi: 他很努力地维护自己的家。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn nǔlì de wéihù zìjǐ de jiā.
examples.english: He works hard to look after his home.

examples.hanzi: 这座老房子需要维修。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò lǎo fángzi xūyào wéixiū.
examples.english: This old house needs repair.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo slips, once used for writing and lists, as in 等 wait, 笔 pen, 笑 laugh.
弟 (dì) gives the exact sound; 弟 also sounds out 梯 tī and 剃 tì.
囗 (enclosure) — the outer box, as in 国 country and 回. The dictionary reading: four walls of a room, with a child (儿) inside; memory aid only, sound-borrowed.
儿 (legs/child) — inside the box, as in 先 and 兄. Memory aid: the shape is simply a box with two legs; it does not explain 'four'.

example.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒmen dìsì cì jiànmiàn.
example.english: This is the fourth time we've met.
example.fact: 第 attaches to a bare cardinal number to build an ordinal (第一 "first", 第二 "second", 第四 "fourth") — without 第, 四 alone just means the cardinal "four," so this one small character is doing all of the "-th" work in a Chinese ordinal.

examples.hanzi: 我住在这栋楼的第四层。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhù zài zhè dòng lóu de dìsì céng.
examples.english: I live on the fourth floor of this building.

examples.hanzi: 她在比赛中得了第四名。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài bǐsài zhōng dé le dì sì míng.
examples.english: She came in fourth in the competition.

components.note: 疒 (illness) — 疒 is the sickness radical, as in 病, 痛, 痕; 症 is an illness or its symptoms.
正 (zhèng) — same sound — 症 is zhèng, like 正; 正 also sounds out 证 zhèng.

example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng bìng de zhèngzhuàng hěn qīng.
example.english: The symptoms of this illness are mild.
example.fact: 症 is a bound form: 症状 (symptom), 炎症 (inflammation), 失眠症 (insomnia). 后遗症 means sequelae and is also used figuratively for side effects of a policy.

examples.hanzi: 他的病症很严重，要马上去医院。
examples.pinyin: Tā de bìngzhèng hěn yánzhòng, yào mǎshàng qù yīyuàn.
examples.english: His illness is serious; he must go to the hospital right away.

examples.hanzi: 她有失眠的症状。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu shīmián de zhèngzhuàng.
examples.english: She has symptoms of insomnia.

components.note: 鬼 (ghost) — spirits and the unseen: 魂, 魅, 愧; 魔 is a demon.
麻 (má) is a near sound match for mó; also in 磨 mó and 摩 mó.
鬼 (ghost) — a creature with a big head and a hollow body. As a radical it brings in spirits: 魂 soul, 魔 demon, 愧 ashamed.

example.hanzi: 他在梦里看到一个魔鬼。
example.pinyin: Tā zài mèng lǐ kàndào yí gè móguǐ.
example.english: He saw a devil in his dream.
example.fact: 魔 is itself built on top of 鬼 ("ghost, spirit") — 魔鬼 stacks two already-supernatural characters into one word, the same reinforcing strategy behind 喜欢 ("to like", stacking two "joy" characters); 鬼's own shape, a strange 田-like head over spindly 儿-like legs, is a fairly literal picture of a ghostly figure.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们说床底下有魔鬼。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen shuō chuáng dǐxia yǒu móguǐ.
examples.english: The kids say there's a devil under the bed.

examples.hanzi: 这部电影里的魔鬼看起来很可怕。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng lǐ de móguǐ kàn qǐlái hěn kěpà.
examples.english: The devil in this movie looks very scary.

components.note: 子 (child) — 子 means child, as in 孩, 孙; 孤 is a lone child, an orphan.
瓜 (guā) — near sound — 孤 is gū; 瓜 also sounds out 狐 hú and 弧 hú.
犭 (dog, beast) — animals: 狗, 猫, 狼; 独 first meant a solitary animal, then alone.
The old sound part 蜀 (shǔ) is also in 属 shǔ, 烛 zhú and 触 chù; simplified 独 shows 虫 instead.

example.pinyin: Lǎorén yí gè rén zhù, hěn gūdú.
example.english: The old man lives alone; he is very lonely.
example.fact: 孤 originally named a fatherless child, an orphan (built from 子 "child" with the phonetic 瓜), while 独 carries a sense of "single, solitary"; 孤独 combines "orphaned" with "alone" into today's word for the emotional state of loneliness, not just physical solitude.

examples.hanzi: 一个人在国外,他常常觉得孤独。
examples.pinyin: Yí ge rén zài guówài, tā chángcháng juéde gūdú.
examples.english: Being alone abroad, he often feels lonely.

examples.hanzi: 她喜欢孤独,不爱热闹。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan gūdú, bú ài rènao.
examples.english: She likes solitude and doesn't enjoy crowds.

components.note: 内 (inside) — a person or something entering 入 inside an enclosure 冂: inside, as in 内容.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室: a building holds things.
谷 (valley) — a hollow that holds: 容 is to hold or allow.

example.pinyin: Zhè běn shū de nèiróng hěn yǒuqù.
example.english: The content of this book is very interesting.
example.fact: 容 on its own already means "to hold, to contain" (built from 宀, "roof," the image of a house holding things inside) — 内容 pairs that "container" sense with 内 ("inside") to literally mean "what is held inside," giving the word its modern sense of "content."

examples.hanzi: 这份报告的内容很详细。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn bàogào de nèiróng hěn xiángxì.
examples.english: The content of this report is very detailed.

examples.hanzi: 我没听懂他讲的内容。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ méi tīng dǒng tā jiǎng de nèiróng.
examples.english: I didn't understand what he said.

components.note: 工 (tool, work) — originally a carpenter's square held in a hand — the same word as 矩; 巨 also sounds out 距 jù and 拒 jù.
大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.

example.pinyin: Zhè kē shù fēicháng jùdà.
example.english: This tree is enormous.
example.fact: 巨 and 大 both independently mean roughly "big, great" — 巨大 doubles up two near-synonyms for size into one intensified adjective, the same word-building strategy behind 喜欢 and 应该; 巨 itself is traditionally read as a picture of a hand gripping an oversized carpenter's square.

examples.hanzi: 一块巨大的石头挡住了路。
examples.pinyin: Yí kuài jùdà de shítou dǎng zhù le lù.
examples.english: A huge rock blocked the road.

examples.hanzi: 这个城市这些年发生了巨大的变化。
examples.pinyin: Zhège chéngshì zhèxiē nián fāshēng le jùdà de biànhuà.
examples.english: This city has undergone huge changes in recent years.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室.
玉 (jade) — jade kept under a roof: treasure. The traditional 寶 also had 贝 (cowrie, money).
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室.
玉 (jade) — jade kept under a roof: treasure. The traditional 寶 also had 贝 (cowrie, money).

example.pinyin: Māma bàozhe bǎobao.
example.english: Mom is holding the baby.
example.fact: 宝 originally meant "treasure" (a roof 宀 sheltering jade 玉 inside) — reduplicating it into 宝宝 turns a noun for a precious object into an affectionate term for a baby or loved one, the same doubling pattern seen in 谢谢 and 瞧瞧, just applied to a noun instead of a verb.

examples.hanzi: 我们的宝宝刚学会走路。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de bǎobao gāng xuéhuì zǒulù.
examples.english: Our baby has just learned to walk.

examples.hanzi: 宝宝,该睡觉了。
examples.pinyin: Bǎobao, gāi shuìjiào le.
examples.english: Sweetie, it's time to go to sleep.

components.note: 心 (heart) — 心 marks thought and feelings, as in 想, 急; 惩 is to make someone feel sorry through punishment.
征 (zhēng) — near sound — 惩 is chéng; 征 also sounds out 证 zhèng.
刂 (knife) — 刂 is 刀 (knife) as in 到, 别, 利; punishing was once done by cutting.
讠 (speech) — 讠 (言, words) — 罚 originally also meant scolding.

example.hanzi: 迟到的学生被老师惩罚了。
example.pinyin: Chídào de xuésheng bèi lǎoshī chéngfá le.
example.english: The students who were late were punished by the teacher.
example.fact: 惩 carries the heart radical 心, tying punishment to its effect on one's conscience, while 罚's components (a net 罒 plus a blade 刂) point to catching wrongdoing and carrying out a penalty — together 惩罚 layers the psychological and the punitive sides of punishment into one word.

examples.hanzi: 犯了错就要接受惩罚。
examples.pinyin: Fàn le cuò jiù yào jiēshòu chéngfá.
examples.english: If you make a mistake, you have to accept the punishment.

examples.hanzi: 法律会惩罚做坏事的人。
examples.pinyin: Fǎlǜ huì chéngfá zuò huàishì de rén.
examples.english: The law punishes people who do bad things.

components.note: 力 (strength) — with 口 mouth: adding strength by words, hence to add, to increase. 加 also in 架 jià and 驾 jià.
上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.

example.hanzi: 价格加上运费一共一百元。
example.pinyin: Jiàgé jiāshàng yùnfèi yígòng yìbǎi yuán.
example.english: The price plus shipping comes to one hundred yuan in total.
example.fact: 加 pictures adding one's physical strength (力) together with supportive words (口) — literally "muscle plus voice" — while 上 here works as a directional complement meaning "on top of, additionally"; 加上 stacks "to add" onto "on top" to introduce one more item or reason, much like English "plus" or "on top of that."

examples.hanzi: 这些菜加上米饭,一共五十块。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē cài jiā shàng mǐfàn, yígòng wǔshí kuài.
examples.english: These dishes plus rice come to fifty yuan in total.

examples.hanzi: 他很聪明,加上又很努力,所以成绩很好。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn cōngmíng, jiā shàng yòu hěn nǔlì, suǒyǐ chéngjì hěn hǎo.
examples.english: He is clever and, on top of that, hard-working, so his grades are good.

meanings: (lit. and fig.) to open a door

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — in 開 two hands lift the bar of a gate; 开 is the simplified shape. Compare 关 (close).
门 (gate) — a picture of a two-leaf door; as a radical it frames characters of doors and openings — 开, 关, 问, 间.

example.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn jǐ diǎn kāimén?
example.english: What time does this shop open?
example.fact: 开门 extends beyond its literal sense of unlatching a door to mean "opening for business" — the moment a shop's actual door swings open each day stands in for the more abstract idea of a business being open, a very physical image (per 开's own etymology, hands 廾 lifting away a latch 一) doing double duty.

examples.hanzi: 有人在敲门,你去开门吧。
examples.pinyin: Yǒu rén zài qiāo mén, nǐ qù kāimén ba.
examples.english: Someone's knocking, go open the door.

examples.hanzi: 银行早上九点开门。
examples.pinyin: Yínháng zǎoshang jiǔ diǎn kāimén.
examples.english: The bank opens at nine in the morning.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — 艹 marks plants; 蓝 is the indigo plant from which blue dye was made.
监 (jiān) — loose hint — 蓝 is lán; 监 also sounds out 篮 lán and 滥 làn.
⺈ (bent person) — a person's figure, the top part of 色. Old story: a person (⺈) sitting on 巴 shows how feelings colour the face, hence 'colour, look'; treat as a memory aid.
巴 (bā) — the lower part; dictionary reads the pair as 'what a person desires'. Memory aid: a face reddening with feeling is a 'colour'.

example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan lánsè de tiānkōng.
example.english: He likes the blue sky.
example.fact: 蓝 originally named the indigo plant itself (built from 艹, "grass, plant") before it came to mean the blue color extracted from it — a dye-plant's name becoming the color word, the same shift English makes when "orange" the color takes its name from the fruit.

examples.hanzi: 她今天穿了一件蓝色的外套。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīntiān chuān le yí jiàn lánsè de wàitào.
examples.english: She is wearing a blue jacket today.

examples.hanzi: 大海是深蓝色的。
examples.pinyin: Dàhǎi shì shēn lánsè de.
examples.english: The sea is deep blue.

components.note: 辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 送; 退 is to step back.
凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.

example.pinyin: Tā juédìng tuìchū bǐsài.
example.english: He decided to withdraw from the competition.
example.fact: 退 (辶 "to walk" plus the phonetic 艮) pictures physically moving backward, while 出 pictures a sprout growing up and out of a container; 退出 combines "stepping back" with "going out," making it equally natural for leaving a competition, an organization, or, in modern usage, logging out of an app.

examples.hanzi: 你可以随时退出这个群。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ suíshí tuìchū zhège qún.
examples.english: You can leave this group at any time.

examples.hanzi: 他受伤后不得不退出球队。
examples.pinyin: Tā shòushāng hòu bù dé bù tuìchū qiúduì.
examples.english: After getting hurt, he had to leave the team.

components.note: 鬼 (ghost) — a creature with a big head and a hollow body. As a radical it brings in spirits: 魂 soul, 魔 demon, 愧 ashamed.
鬼 (ghost) — spirits and the unseen: 魔 demon, 魅 charm, 魄 spirit; 魂 is the soul.
云 (yún) is a near sound match for hún.

example.hanzi: 她说这栋房子里有鬼魂。
example.pinyin: Tā shuō zhè dòng fángzi lǐ yǒu guǐhún.
example.english: She says there's a ghost in this house.
example.fact: 魂 is literally built on top of 鬼 ("ghost") itself, with 云 ("cloud") lending only its sound — 鬼魂 pairs the picture-word for "ghost" with the more abstract "soul, spirit," reflecting the old folk belief that a person's 魂 could linger on as a 鬼 after death.

examples.hanzi: 大家都说那座老房子里有鬼魂。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu shuō nà zuò lǎo fángzi lǐ yǒu guǐhún.
examples.english: Everyone says there are ghosts in that old house.

examples.hanzi: 他梦到了爷爷的鬼魂。
examples.pinyin: Tā mèng dào le yéye de guǐhún.
examples.english: He dreamed of his grandfather's ghost.

components.note: 寸 (hand, inch) — hands and measuring, as in 寻 seek, 导 lead, 射 shoot; 对 faces someone or matches a pair. 又 here only stands in for the left side of 對.
手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.

example.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ de wǎngqiú duìshǒu.
example.english: He is my tennis opponent.
example.fact: 对 carries a core sense of "facing, matching, corresponding to" (from two hands meeting) — 对手 literally means "a matching hand," the person whose skill is set directly against yours, whether in sport, business, or debate.

examples.hanzi: 我们在决赛中遇到了强大的对手。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài juésài zhōng yùdào le qiángdà de duìshǒu.
examples.english: We met a tough opponent in the final.

examples.hanzi: 别小看你的对手。
examples.pinyin: Bié xiǎokàn nǐ de duìshǒu.
examples.english: Don't underestimate your opponent.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — the right-hand side. Usually about cutting (到, 别, 利), but not in 前: it is a later corruption of the old picture.
舟 (boat) — hidden in the old form: a foot on a boat moving ahead, so 'in front, forward'. Usual explanation, though the modern shape hides it.
辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 近, 送: to go forward.
井 stands in for 隹 of 進, a loose clue only.

example.pinyin: Jūnduì jìxù qiánjìn.
example.english: The army continued to advance.
example.fact: 进 (辶 "to walk" plus the phonetic 井) already means "to advance, to enter" on its own — 前进 reinforces it by adding 前 ("forward, ahead"), the same reinforcing-synonym pattern seen in 喜欢 and 巨大, just built from two motion-related characters instead.

examples.hanzi: 不管遇到什么困难,我们都要前进。
examples.pinyin: Bùguǎn yùdào shénme kùnnan, wǒmen dōu yào qiánjìn.
examples.english: No matter what difficulties we meet, we have to keep moving forward.

examples.hanzi: 向前进,不要回头!
examples.pinyin: Xiàng qiánjìn, bú yào huítóu!
examples.english: Go forward, don't look back!

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings and thought, as in 想 think, 思 ponder, 急 anxious; in 怎 it is only loosely linked to the question sense.
乍 (zhà) is a loose sound clue for zěn; 乍 also sounds out 作 zuò, 昨 zuó and 炸 zhà.

example.pinyin: Nǐ zěnme qù xuéxiào?
example.english: How do you get to school?
example.fact: 怎 never appears alone: it is in 怎么 (how / why), 怎样 (how) and 怎么样 (how is it?). 怎么 can ask for a method (怎么去) or express surprise (你怎么来了, why are you here?).

examples.hanzi: 你怎么还没睡？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zěnme hái méi shuì?
examples.english: Why aren't you asleep yet?

examples.hanzi: 这个词怎么写？
examples.pinyin: Zhège cí zěnme xiě?
examples.english: How do you write this word?

components.note: 夭 (young, bending person) — the top part, as in 笑 smile. Dictionary story: a person on stilts, so tall and lofty. In 乔治 George it is just a sound.
氵 (water radical, 三点水) — liquids and flow: 河, 汤, 酒; 治 first meant controlling water, then governing and curing.
台 (tái) is only a loose sound hint; the same part is in 始 shǐ and 胎 tāi.

example.hanzi: 乔治是一个很常见的英文名字。
example.pinyin: Qiáozhì shì yí gè hěn chángjiàn de Yīngwén míngzi.
example.english: George is a very common English name.
example.fact: 乔治 is a pure sound-based transliteration of the English name "George," pairing 乔 (whose own etymology pictures someone walking tall on stilts, "lofty") with 治 ("to govern") — chosen purely for their pronunciation, not their meaning, the same phonetic strategy behind 华盛顿 ("Washington," rank 1201 in this batch).

examples.hanzi: 我哥哥的英文名字叫乔治。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gēge de Yīngwén míngzi jiào Qiáozhì.
examples.english: My older brother's English name is George.

examples.hanzi: 乔治今天早上给我打了个电话。
examples.pinyin: Qiáozhì jīntiān zǎoshang gěi wǒ dǎ le ge diànhuà.
examples.english: George called me this morning.

components.note: 礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — gods, rites and blessings: 礼 ritual, 福 fortune, 祝 wish; here 神 god or spirit.
申 (shēn) gives the sound (shén, tone differs); also in 伸 shēn stretch and 绅 shēn.
奇 (qí) is a sound clue for 骑 qí, 寄 jì, 椅 yǐ and 崎 qí; as a word it means strange or remarkable.

example.pinyin: Dàzìrán zhēn shì shénqí.
example.english: Nature is truly magical.
example.fact: 神 ("god, spirit") pairs with 奇 ("strange, remarkable" — traditionally pictured as someone riding in an unusual way) to describe something so remarkable it feels touched by the divine; 神奇 reads as more wondrous and awe-struck than the more hidden, secretive 神秘 ("mysterious," also in this batch, rank 1203), even though both start with the same 神.

examples.hanzi: 这个魔术真神奇,我完全看不懂。
examples.pinyin: Zhège móshù zhēn shénqí, wǒ wánquán kàn bù dǒng.
examples.english: This magic trick is amazing, I can't understand it at all.

examples.hanzi: 这种药有神奇的效果。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng yào yǒu shénqí de xiàoguǒ.
examples.english: This medicine has miraculous effects.

components.note: 牛 (ox, cattle) — 牛 is cattle, as in 牺, 牲, 物; 牧 shows a hand with a stick 攵 herding cattle.
攵 (tap, strike) — 攵 is a hand with a stick, as in 教, 放.
师 (shī) is a sound clue for 狮 shī (lion) and 筛 shāi; as a word it means master or teacher.

example.pinyin: Tā shì zhège jiàotáng de mùshī.
example.english: He is the pastor of this church.
example.fact: 牧 pictures a hand with a stick (攵) driving an ox (牛) — literally "herding" — extended metaphorically in 牧师 to a religious leader who "shepherds" a congregation, echoing the same herder/flock metaphor English uses for "pastor" (from Latin pastor, "shepherd").

examples.hanzi: 牧师在教堂里为新人祝福。
examples.pinyin: Mùshī zài jiàotáng lǐ wèi xīnrén zhùfú.
examples.english: The pastor gave a blessing to the newlyweds in the church.

examples.hanzi: 这位牧师每个星期天都会讲道。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi mùshī měi ge xīngqītiān dōu huì jiǎng dào.
examples.english: This pastor gives a sermon every Sunday.

components.note: 年 (year) — first drawn as a person carrying harvested grain: one harvest per year. Seen in 今年, 去年, 年轻.
纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 线, 给; 级 first meant the order of threads, then rank.
及 (jí) sounds exactly like 级; also 极 jí, 吸 xī.

example.pinyin: Wǒ nǚ'ér xiànzài shàng sān niánjí.
example.english: My daughter is now in third grade.
example.fact: 级, whose thread radical 纟 originally named a rank or strand of silk, extends that "strand/rank" image in 年级 — literally "year-rank" — to name the specific step of schooling a student has reached in a given year.

examples.hanzi: 你弟弟在几年级?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ dìdi zài jǐ niánjí?
examples.english: What grade is your younger brother in?

examples.hanzi: 我们是同一个年级的。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen shì tóng yí ge niánjí de.
examples.english: We are in the same grade.

components.note: 王 (jade) — 王 on the left is 玉 (jade) as in 玩, 球, 现; 环 is a jade ring, as in 环境.
土 (earth) — 土 is earth and land, as in 地, 城, 块; 境 is a stretch of land, a border or condition.
竟 (jìng) — same sound — 境 is jìng, like 竟; 竟 also sounds out 镜 jìng.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen yīnggāi bǎohù huánjìng.
example.english: We should protect the environment.
example.fact: 环 originally named a round jade ring or bracelet (built from 王, a variant of 玉, "jade") — extended metaphorically to anything that encircles, 环境 combines that "surrounding ring" image with 境 ("territory, boundary") to give the modern word for one's surrounding environment or circumstances.

examples.hanzi: 这里的环境又安静又干净。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de huánjìng yòu ānjìng yòu gānjìng.
examples.english: The environment here is quiet and clean.

examples.hanzi: 我刚来这里,还不太适应环境。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gāng lái zhèlǐ, hái bú tài shìyìng huánjìng.
examples.english: I've just arrived and haven't adapted to my surroundings yet.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 提 is to lift or carry in the hand.
是 (shì) is a loose sound hint; the same part is in 题 tí and 堤 dī.
至 (arrive) — 到 is to arrive.
刂 is the knife form 刀 (dāo), a close sound clue for dào; 到 itself sounds out 倒 dǎo/dào.

example.pinyin: Tā zài xìn lǐ tídào nǐ le.
example.english: He mentioned you in the letter.
example.fact: 提 (a hand 扌 lifting something up) contributes the image of "raising, bringing up," while 到 means "to arrive, to reach" — 提到 literally "raises [a topic] until it arrives [in the conversation]," a fairly direct compositional route to the abstract sense of "to mention."

examples.hanzi: 他从来没有提到过自己的家人。
examples.pinyin: Tā cónglái méiyǒu tídào guo zìjǐ de jiārén.
examples.english: He has never mentioned his family.

examples.hanzi: 老师今天提到了下周的考试。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī jīntiān tídào le xià zhōu de kǎoshì.
examples.english: The teacher brought up next week's exam today.

components.note: 木 (tree) — the bottom part, as in 林 forest and 树 tree; in old 雜 the tree or clothing bits show collecting many things. Treat as a loose hint only.
九 (nine) — the top part; 杂 is simplified from 雜. Memory aid: nine kinds of wood piled up, a mix.
禾 (grain) — crops, as in 秋 autumn, 租 rent, 和 and 秒 second; 种 is seed or to plant.
中 (zhōng) is a close sound clue for zhǒng/zhòng.

example.pinyin: Zhè zhī gǒu shì zázhǒng.
example.english: This dog is a mixed breed.
example.fact: 种 (grain 禾 plus the phonetic 中) literally means "seed, to plant" — 杂种 literally "mixed seed," a term from breeding and agriculture for a cross-bred animal or plant; that same literal "mixed seed" image is also what gives the word its much harsher, vulgar insult sense in modern slang, a jump in register worth knowing before using it casually.

examples.hanzi: 这只小猫是杂种,不是纯种猫。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī xiǎo māo shì zázhǒng, bú shì chúnzhǒng māo.
examples.english: This kitten is a mixed breed, not a purebred.

examples.hanzi: 杂种狗往往比较健康。
examples.pinyin: Zázhǒng gǒu wǎngwǎng bǐjiào jiànkāng.
examples.english: Mixed-breed dogs are often healthier.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and roles: 你, 他, 位; 代 is one person replacing another, then a generation.
弋 (yì) is only a loose hint; 代 itself sounds out 袋 dài and 贷 dài.

example.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ dài wǒ qù ma?
example.english: Can you go in my place?
example.fact: 代 means to substitute: 代替, 代表 (represent), and the polite 代我向他问好 (give him my regards). It also means generation or era: 现代, 年代, 下一代.

examples.hanzi: 老师今天不在，我来代课。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī jīntiān bú zài, wǒ lái dàikè.
examples.english: The teacher is away today, so I'm filling in.

examples.hanzi: 这是年轻一代的想法。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì niánqīng yí dài de xiǎngfǎ.
examples.english: This is the thinking of the younger generation.

components.note: 癶 (two feet) — two feet stepping upward: 登 is to climb or board, as in 登山 mountain-climbing.
豆 (dòu) is only a loose sound hint; 登 dēng also sounds out 灯 dēng and 凳 dèng.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōumò qù dēngshān.
example.english: We are going mountain climbing this weekend.
example.fact: 登 is formal climbing (登山), boarding (登机) and entering information: 登录 (to log in). 登陆 is a homophone meaning to land or to come ashore, so both are dēnglù. 登报 means to publish in a newspaper.

examples.hanzi: 他登上了山顶。
examples.pinyin: Tā dēngshàng le shāndǐng.
examples.english: He climbed to the top of the mountain.

examples.hanzi: 请在网站上登记你的名字。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài wǎngzhàn shang dēngjì nǐ de míngzi.
examples.english: Please register your name on the website.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — 刂 is 刀 (knife) on the right, as in 到, 别, 利; 刺 is to stab.
朿 (cì) — 朿 is a thorn and gives the sound — 刺 is cì, same syllable.
氵 (water radical, 三点水) — water and liquids: 河, 海, 汤; 激 is water surging up, then to stir up.
敫 (jiǎo) is only a loose sound clue for jī.

example.hanzi: 蹦极是一项很刺激的运动。
example.pinyin: Bèngjí shì yí xiàng hěn cìjī de yùndòng.
example.english: Bungee jumping is a very thrilling sport.
example.fact: 刺 pictures a blade 刂 piercing something sharp (its phonetic 朿 is an exact sound match for cì) — 刺激 combines "to prick, to stab" with 激 ("water surging forcefully") into one word that covers both the negative sense of "to provoke, to irritate" and the more neutral or positive sense of "to stimulate, to thrill," depending on context.

examples.hanzi: 别刺激他,他现在心情不好。
examples.pinyin: Bié cìjī tā, tā xiànzài xīnqíng bù hǎo.
examples.english: Don't provoke him, he's in a bad mood now.

examples.hanzi: 这部电影太刺激了,我一直没敢眨眼。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng tài cìjī le, wǒ yìzhí méi gǎn zhǎyǎn.
examples.english: This movie was so thrilling that I didn't dare to blink.

components.note: 戈 (halberd) — a weapon radical, as in 战 war and 成. 我 began as a picture of a jagged-bladed weapon; the pronoun "I" is a later borrowing of the sound.
会 (meet, can) — simplified from 會, a lid on a container: bringing things together; hence meeting, then "can" (huì).

example.pinyin: Wǒ huì nǔlì xuéxí Zhōngwén.
example.english: I will study Chinese hard.
example.fact: 会 alone already carries two distinct senses that 我会 inherits directly depending on context — a learned ability ("I know how to," as in 我会说中文, "I can speak Chinese") and a prediction about intention or the future ("I will," as in this example) — the same verb doing quite different grammatical jobs depending on what follows it.

examples.hanzi: 放心吧,我会帮你的。
examples.pinyin: Fàngxīn ba, wǒ huì bāng nǐ de.
examples.english: Don't worry, I'll help you.

examples.hanzi: 我会开车,但是我不会游泳。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ huì kāichē, dànshì wǒ bú huì yóuyǒng.
examples.english: I can drive, but I can't swim.

components.note: 见 (see) — 见 as in 现, 观, 觉; 规 first meant a compass, the drawing tool that sets the standard — hence rules, as in 规矩 compass and square.
夫 (fū) — loose sound hint — 规 is guī.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家 home, 安 safe, 客 guest; settling down under a roof.
正 (zhèng, upright; the lower part is written 疋) is a loose sound clue for dìng; also in 证 zhèng and 政 zhèng.

example.pinyin: Gōngsī yǒu yángé de guīdìng.
example.english: The company has strict regulations.
example.fact: 规 originally named a compass, a craftsman's tool for drawing perfect circles (linked to 见, "to see, observe") — 规定 combines that tool-for-precision image with 定 ("to fix, to settle") to describe rules that have been measured out and fixed in place.

examples.hanzi: 学校规定,上课时不能玩手机。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào guīdìng, shàngkè shí bù néng wán shǒujī.
examples.english: The school rules that phones cannot be used during class.

examples.hanzi: 按照规定,我们要提前一个小时到。
examples.pinyin: Ànzhào guīdìng, wǒmen yào tíqián yí ge xiǎoshí dào.
examples.english: According to the rules, we have to arrive an hour early.

components.note: 几 (low table) — what you lean on. 凭 means to lean on, so to rely on (凭证 proof, 凭什么 on what basis).
任 (to trust, to bear) — the top part. The dictionary story is leaning on a table; its sound does not match píng. Memory aid: lean on something you trust.

example.pinyin: Nǐ píng shénme zhèyàng shuō?
example.english: On what basis do you say that?
example.fact: 凭什么 means "on what grounds?" and is often a challenge. 凭 is also "to rely on": 凭票入场 (admission by ticket). It forms 文凭 (diploma) and 凭证 (voucher).

examples.hanzi: 你不能凭一张照片就下结论。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bù néng píng yì zhāng zhàopiàn jiù xià jiélùn.
examples.english: You can't draw a conclusion from just one photo.

examples.hanzi: 进门要凭票。
examples.pinyin: Jìnmén yào píng piào.
examples.english: You need a ticket to enter.
